name: Kylian Mbappé
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2018 FIFA World Cup with France at age 19, scoring in the final against Croatia.
early_history_summary: Mbappé grew up in Bondy, a suburb of Paris, and joined the Clairefontaine national training academy at age 12. He signed for AS Monaco's academy at 14, made his Ligue 1 debut at 16 (breaking Thierry Henry's record as Monaco's youngest player), and signed his first professional contract at 17. By 18 he had transferred to PSG and by 19 he was a World Cup winner.
family_context_summary: Born in Paris to a football coach father (Wilfried Mbappé) and a former handball player mother (Fayza Lamari); grew up in the Parisian suburb of Bondy with access to local football infrastructure.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a football coach at AS Bondy and mother was a handball player, providing direct sporting domain immersion from early childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Clairefontaine academy, football family, Bondy youth system, early prodigy
evidence_summary: Mbappé benefited from a football-coach father and handball-player mother who immersed him in sport from childhood. He entered the Clairefontaine national academy at 12, joined Monaco's academy at 14, and made his professional debut at 16. His extraordinary pace and technical ability marked him as a generational talent, culminating in a World Cup win at 19. The combination of family sporting background, elite academy pipeline, and prodigious physical talent created an unusually accelerated trajectory.
starting_point: Born in Paris to a football coach father and handball player mother; grew up in the working-class suburb of Bondy with strong local football infrastructure.
current_position: Plays for Real Madrid and captains the France national team; estimated net worth ~$180M; one of the world's highest-paid athletes.

trajectory.event: Made Ligue 1 debut for AS Monaco, becoming the club's youngest ever player.
Transferred to Paris Saint-Germain, initially on loan, becoming one of the most expensive players in history.
Won the FIFA World Cup with France, scoring in the final against Croatia.
Scored a hat-trick in the World Cup final against Argentina, though France lost on penalties.
Joined Real Madrid on a free transfer after seven seasons at PSG.
Won the European Golden Shoe as top scorer in European domestic leagues and won the Champions League with Real Madrid.

name: Juliane Koepcke
milestone_by_age_26: No material professional biology milestone by age 26 found; fame derives from surviving a plane crash at 17, not from a scientific achievement. She graduated in biology from the University of Kiel in 1980 (age 25-26) but her PhD and notable bat research came later.
early_history_summary: Koepcke was raised by zoologist parents at the Panguana research station in the Peruvian Amazon from age 14. She survived the LANSA Flight 508 crash in December 1971 at age 17, then returned to Germany to study biology at the University of Kiel, graduating in 1980.
family_context_summary: Daughter of renowned German zoologists Hans-Wilhelm and Maria Koepcke, who established the Panguana research station in Peru.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were zoologists, providing deep early immersion in biological field research and Amazonian ecology.
evidence_summary: Koepcke's fame stems from surviving a plane crash at 17, not from a professional milestone. She later became a mammalogist specializing in bats, earning a doctorate from LMU Munich and publishing her thesis in 1987. By age 26 she had only completed her undergraduate biology degree at Kiel, with no notable scientific achievement yet.

name: R. D. Burman
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted as an independent music director with the Hindi film Chhote Nawab (1961) at age 22, which was a box office hit.
early_history_summary: Born to legendary film composer S.D. Burman, R.D. Burman (nicknamed Pancham) showed musical talent early, composing tunes used in his father's films as a child (Funtoosh, 1956; Pyaasa, 1957). He trained in tabla, sarod under Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, and sitar, and assisted his father before getting his own break with Chhote Nawab in 1961.
secondary_engine: Technical depth in Indian classical music
family_context_summary: Born to legendary Hindi film composer S.D. Burman and singer/dancer Meera Dev Burman in Calcutta; raised partly by grandmother while father worked in Bombay; family experienced urban poverty early on.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father S.D. Burman was one of India's most prominent film music composers, directly training R.D. in classical music and providing entry into the Bollywood film industry.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father SD Burman, Bollywood access, classical training, early composing
evidence_summary: R.D. Burman inherited deep musical domain access through his father S.D. Burman, one of India's top film composers. He composed tunes as a child that his father used in films, trained under eminent gurus including Ali Akbar Khan, and assisted his father on numerous films before debuting independently at 22 with Chhote Nawab. The family-domain apprenticeship gave him both technical depth and industry entry that would have been nearly impossible to replicate independently.
starting_point: Born to legendary film music composer S.D. Burman in Calcutta; raised partly by grandmother in urban poverty while father worked in Bombay film industry.
current_position: Died on January 4, 1994 at age 54; final role as one of Bollywood's most influential and prolific music composers with 331 films scored.

trajectory.event: Composed first tune used in father S.D. Burman's film Funtoosh.
Played harmonica on father's film Solva Saal, including the hit song 'Hai Apna Dil To Awara.'
Debuted as independent music director with Chhote Nawab, a box office hit.
Breakthrough with Teesri Manzil soundtrack, establishing him as a leading Bollywood composer.
Composed landmark soundtrack for Sholay, one of Bollywood's most iconic films.
Died on January 4 in Mumbai after a career spanning over 331 films.

name: Daphne Caruana Galizia
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. She began writing a column for the Sunday Times of Malta in 1987-88 at age 23-24, but her major investigative reputation and international fame came decades later with the Panama Papers and her assassination in 2017.
early_history_summary: Born in Sliema, Malta, Caruana Galizia began her journalism career as a columnist for the Sunday Times of Malta in 1987-88. She later helped establish The Malta Independent and enrolled at the University of Malta as a mature student at 28, studying archaeology.
family_context_summary: Born to businessman Michael Alfred Vella and Rose Marie Vella in Sliema, Malta; described as growing up in a 'normal, middle-class' family.
evidence_summary: Caruana Galizia began her column at the Sunday Times of Malta at 23-24, making her Malta's first woman columnist publishing under her own name. However, this was a career start rather than a material achievement milestone. Her international reputation was built through decades of investigative journalism, culminating in her Panama Papers reporting and assassination by car bomb in 2017.

name: Jonny Nilsson
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1963 World Allround Speed Skating Championship at age 20, setting three world records (5,000m, 10,000m, and allround points), and won Olympic gold in the 10,000m at age 21 in 1964.
early_history_summary: Nilsson debuted at the 1962 World Championships at 19, winning the 10,000m and placing second in the 5,000m, earning the Oscar Mathisen Award. The following year he won the world allround title with three world records, and in 1964 he confirmed his dominance with Olympic gold in the 10,000m at Innsbruck.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swedish skating tradition, early world championship, long-distance specialization
evidence_summary: Nilsson emerged as a world-class speed skater at 19, winning the 10,000m at the 1962 World Championships. At 20 he won the World Allround title with three world records, and at 21 he won Olympic gold. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources, but the Swedish speed skating tradition and his club Bofors Cykelklubb provided a performance pipeline. His achievements were driven by exceptional endurance and early specialization in long-distance skating.
starting_point: Born in Gothenburg, Sweden; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on June 22, 2022 at age 79; later worked as a real estate agent and was a political candidate for the Christian Democrats.

trajectory.event: Won 10,000m and placed second in 5,000m at World Championships; awarded Oscar Mathisen Award.
Won World Allround Championship in Karuizawa, setting three world records and becoming first Swede to win since 1955.
Won Olympic gold in 10,000m at Innsbruck Winter Olympics.
Broke 5,000m world record in Oslo despite finishing 4th at World Allround Championships.
Won bronze at World Allround Championships in Gothenburg.
Retired from competitive speed skating after Grenoble Olympics.
Died on June 22 in Sweden.

name: Andrea de Cesaris
milestone_by_age_26: Took pole position at the 1982 United States Grand Prix West at Long Beach at age 22, becoming the youngest pole sitter in Formula 1 history at the time.
early_history_summary: De Cesaris was a multiple karting champion who finished second in the 1979 British Formula Three Championship at 20, stepped up to Formula 2 with Ron Dennis's Project 4 team in 1980, and made his Formula 1 debut with Alfa Romeo late in 1980 at 21. In 1982 he took pole position at Long Beach, becoming F1's youngest ever pole sitter.
secondary_engine: Family business connections with Philip Morris
family_context_summary: Family had business connections with Philip Morris (Marlboro), which helped arrange his F1 debut with Alfa Romeo and subsequent McLaren seat.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond family's Philip Morris business connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Philip Morris family connections, karting champion, F3 runner-up, Ron Dennis mentorship
evidence_summary: De Cesaris leveraged family business connections with Philip Morris to secure his F1 debut with Alfa Romeo in 1980 and a McLaren seat in 1981. He was a multiple karting champion and F3 runner-up by 20, showing genuine speed. His pole position at Long Beach in 1982 at age 22 made him the youngest pole sitter in F1 history at the time. However, his career was marred by frequent crashes and he never won a race in 208 starts.
starting_point: Born in Rome, Italy; family had business connections with Philip Morris that facilitated his motorsport career.
current_position: Died on October 5, 2014 at age 55 in a motorcycle accident in Rome; final role as retired F1 driver with 208 Grand Prix starts.

trajectory.event: Finished second in the British Formula Three Championship.
Made Formula 1 debut with Alfa Romeo at the Canadian Grand Prix.
Took pole position at the US Grand Prix West in Long Beach, becoming F1's youngest ever pole sitter.
Scored first F1 podium finishes with Alfa Romeo and consistently qualified in the top 10.
Retired from Formula 1 after 208 Grand Prix starts without a victory.
Died on October 5 in a motorcycle accident in Rome.

name: Stan Mikita
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Stanley Cup with the Chicago Blackhawks in 1961 at age 21, leading the playoffs in goals, and won the Art Ross Trophy as NHL leading scorer in 1963-64 at age 23.
early_history_summary: Born in Slovakia, Mikita was adopted by his aunt and uncle and moved to St. Catharines, Ontario at age 8. He played junior hockey for the St. Catharines Teepees, made a brief NHL cameo at 18, and turned pro with the Blackhawks at 19, never playing in the minors. By 21 he was a Stanley Cup champion and by 23 he was the NHL's leading scorer.
primary_leverage_engine: Early specialization and elite team pipeline
family_context_summary: Born Stanislav Guoth in Slovak Republic; adopted by aunt and uncle Anna and Joe Mikita who emigrated to Canada, moving him to St. Catharines, Ontario at age 8 for a better future away from Communist Czechoslovakia.
parent_family_domain_summary: Adoptive uncle Joe Mikita was a working-class immigrant in Canada; no documented hockey domain expertise in the family, but the St. Catharines junior hockey system provided the pipeline.
primary_early_advantage_tags: St. Catharines Teepees, Rudy Pilous mentor, Bobby Hull teammate, junior hockey scoring title
evidence_summary: Mikita's path was shaped by emigration from Slovakia to Canada at 8, where he entered the St. Catharines junior hockey system under coach Rudy Pilous. He won the OHA scoring title as a junior, was called up to the Blackhawks at 18, and turned pro at 19. His partnership with Bobby Hull and the Blackhawks' rising roster created a complementary team dynamic. By 21 he won the Stanley Cup and by 23 he was the NHL's top scorer, driven by early specialization in a Canadian hockey frontier ecosystem.
starting_point: Born in Sokolče, Slovak Republic; adopted by aunt and uncle who brought him to St. Catharines, Ontario at age 8 to escape Communist Czechoslovakia.
current_position: Died on August 7, 2018 at age 78; final role as Chicago Blackhawks ambassador and Hall of Fame center with 1,467 career points.

trajectory.event: Turned pro with the Chicago Blackhawks, skipping the minor leagues entirely.
Won the Stanley Cup with the Blackhawks, leading the playoffs in goals; first Slovak-born player to win the Cup.
Won the Art Ross Trophy as the NHL's leading scorer with 89 points.
Won the Hart Trophy, Art Ross Trophy, and Lady Byng Trophy in the same season, a feat never repeated.
Recorded his 1,000th career NHL point.
Inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame.
Died on August 7 after a long illness.

name: Toyohiro Akiyama
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. He graduated from International Christian University around 1966 and worked for BBC London from 1967-1971, but his famous achievement — becoming the first Japanese person in space — occurred in December 1990 at age 48.
early_history_summary: Akiyama graduated from the International Christian University in Japan and joined TBS (Tokyo Broadcasting System). He worked for the BBC in London from 1967 to 1971 as a journalist, later becoming deputy director of TBS News Division. His space flight came in 1990 when TBS paid for a commercial Soyuz mission.
evidence_summary: Akiyama's historic achievement — becoming the first Japanese national and first journalist in space — occurred in December 1990 at age 48, when TBS paid approximately $10-28 million for a commercial Soyuz flight to Mir. By age 26, he was an early-career journalist working for the BBC in London, with no notable milestone.

name: Héctor Baldassi
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. He began refereeing youth categories in 1991 at age 25, but his first Argentine first division match came in 1998 at age 32 and his international debut in 2000 at age 34.
early_history_summary: Baldassi began his refereeing career in infantiles categories in 1991, progressed through youth and lower divisions throughout the 1990s, and reached the Argentine Primera División in 1998. His international career began in 2000, culminating in officiating at the 2010 FIFA World Cup.
evidence_summary: Baldassi's refereeing career began in 1991 at age 25 in youth categories. He did not reach the Argentine first division until 1998 at 32, and his international debut came in 2000 at 34. His peak achievements — officiating the 2008 Copa Libertadores final and the 2010 FIFA World Cup — all came well after age 26.

name: Sanja Iveković
milestone_by_age_26: Had her first solo exhibition at SC Gallery in Zagreb in 1970 at age 21, and created 'Sweet Violence' (1974) and 'Double Life' (1975), early works now in MoMA's collection.
early_history_summary: Iveković studied graphics at the Zagreb Academy of Fine Arts from 1968 to 1971. Her artistic career began during the Croatian Spring in the early 1970s as part of the New Art Practice movement, pioneering video, conceptual photomontages, and performance. She was the first artist in Croatia to label herself a feminist artist.
family_context_summary: Born in Zagreb, Yugoslavia (now Croatia) in 1949; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Zagreb New Art Practice, feminist art pioneer, conceptual video art, Croatian Spring
evidence_summary: Iveković emerged as an artist during the Croatian Spring in the early 1970s, part of the New Art Practice movement in Yugoslavia that broke from institutional art. She had her first solo show at SC Gallery in Zagreb in 1970 at 21, and created significant early works including 'Sweet Violence' (1974) and 'Double Life' (1975) that are now in MoMA's collection. Her position in the Yugoslav alternative art scene provided a frontier-geography immersion in conceptual and video art practices.
starting_point: Born in Zagreb, Yugoslavia (now Croatia); family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Active artist in Zagreb; considered one of the leading artists from the former Yugoslavia; founding member of multiple women's organizations including the Center for Women's Studies in Zagreb.

trajectory.event: First solo exhibition at SC Gallery in Zagreb.
Created 'Sweet Violence,' an early video art work now in MoMA's collection.
Created 'Double Life,' a landmark photomontage series pairing personal photos with magazine advertisements.
Co-founded Podroom Gallery with Dalibor Martinis, a hub for Croatian artists.
Became a key player at the Centre for Women's Studies in Zagreb since its opening.
First US retrospective 'Personal Cuts' at MoMA, New York.

name: Riccardo Giacconi
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. He earned his PhD in physics in 1954 at 23 and held a Fulbright fellowship and Princeton position, but his pioneering X-ray astronomy work began at AS&E in 1959 at age 28, with the discovery of Sco X-1 in 1962 at age 30.
early_history_summary: Giacconi earned his PhD in physics from the University of Milan in 1954, working on cosmic ray detection. He won a Fulbright fellowship to the US in 1956, worked at Indiana University and then Princeton (1958-59), before joining American Science & Engineering in 1959 where he founded X-ray astronomy.
family_context_summary: Born in Genoa, Italy; spent most of his young life in Milan. Family background not detailed in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Giacconi's Nobel Prize-winning work in X-ray astronomy began in 1959 at age 28 when he joined AS&E, leading to the discovery of Scorpius X-1 in 1962. By age 26, he had a PhD in physics (1954) and was on fellowships in the US, but had not yet begun the work that would define his career. His achievements — founding X-ray astronomy, directing STScI and ESO, and winning the 2002 Nobel Prize in Physics — all came well after age 26.

name: Pēteris Vasks
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. He studied double bass at the Lithuanian Conservatory (1964-1970) and played in orchestras, but did not begin composition studies until 1973 at age 27. His first recognized compositions date from the mid-1970s and his widespread recognition came in the 1990s.
early_history_summary: Vasks was born into a Baptist pastor's family in Aizpute, Latvia. He studied double bass at the Emīls Dārziņš Music School (1959-64) and Lithuanian Conservatory (1964-70), then played in several orchestras. He began composition studies with Valentin Utkin at the Latvian Music Academy in 1973, graduating in 1978.
family_context_summary: Born in Aizpute, Latvia, into the family of a Baptist pastor who was well-known in Latvia; grew up with Baptist church music.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a Baptist pastor, providing early exposure to church music but not formal musical training or industry access.
evidence_summary: Vasks spent his early career as a double bassist in various orchestras (1963-1974) before beginning composition studies at 27. His early compositions from the mid-1970s were student works, and he gained recognition only in the 1990s when Gidon Kremer championed his music. By age 26, he was an orchestral musician with no notable composition milestone.
